title: Recurrent Looped Transformer
relevance_reason: Recurrence runs across tokens (sequence axis) through a decoder stack, not depth iteration at the same position; paper itself draws this line.
one_sentence: Splits eight layers into a parallel causal encoder and a recurrent decoder whose final state feeds the next token, so the computation path grows with sequence length; length-generalizes parity and S5 tracking where an eight-layer Transformer is at chance.
key_contributions: Encoder-decoder split with per-token feedback of the final decoder state (RLT-1) and chunked feedback (RLT-2)
Shows best depth split is task dependent and that feedback is necessary for parity and swap-based S5
Chunked feedback trades parallelism for accuracy

setup.model_sizes: eight logical layers, width 512; RLT-1 26.10-28.73M parameters vs 25.31M Transformer
setup.train_tokens_or_data: synthetic algorithmic tasks (parity trained on 3-40 bits, S5 on 32 operations)
setup.loops_train: no depth loops; recurrence over tokens
setup.benchmarks: addition, parity, modular arithmetic with and without brackets, standard and swap-based S5

claims.claim: Two RLT splits generalize parity from at most 40 training bits to 256 bits with 100% accuracy in every seed while the eight-layer Transformer is at chance.
claims.regime: unmatched (equal layer count, RLT has 3-14% more parameters and more sequential compute)
claims.evidence_quote: Trained on at most 40 bits, RLT splits 5 + 3 and 7 + 1 reach 100 ± 0% parity accuracy at 256 bits in every seed, compared with 50.07 ± 1.63% for the Transformer.

claims.claim: The comparison matches layer count, not parameters or compute.
claims.evidence_quote: Equal layer counts do not match parameters or compute: RLT-1 has 26.10–28.73M parameters, compared with 25.31M for the Transformer (Table 4).

claims.claim: Chunked feedback keeps parity but hurts permutation tracking, so per-token feedback matters for S5.
claims.evidence_quote: Updating the feedback once per four-token chunk lets known tokens in a chunk run in parallel and keeps 64-bit parity at 99%

claims.claim: The authors place RLT outside depth recurrence: depth-recurrent models recur at each position, RLT recurs across tokens.
claims.evidence_quote: These models recur over depth at each position; RLT-1 recurs across tokens, and sharing weights between its encoder and decoder is optional.

numbers.what: Swap-based S5 final-state accuracy at 256 operations, RLT 4+4 vs Transformer
Flat mod-5 accuracy at length 63 after 5,000 steps, RLT 6+2 vs Transformer
numbers.quote: 6 + 2 reaches 93.36 ± 5.69% on flat mod-5 expressions of length 63, compared with 33.20 ± 2.33%

limitations: Small models (about 26-29M) on synthetic tasks only; parameters and compute not matched to the baseline; sequential decoder work per token during training and prefill.
survey_notes: Sec. 13 (sequence-axis recurrence) or Sec. 9 theory-adjacent. Not depth recurrence; belongs next to Feedback Transformer style work. Evidence for the claim that fixed per-token depth limits state tracking, with TC0 vs NC1 motivation. DeepLoop (arXiv 2607.13491) is cited and may be a missing core paper.

title: TAFFY: A Task-Adaptive Tabular Foundation Model with In-Context Diversity
relevance_reason: Applies the same twelve-block ICL Transformer stack L times to support and query rows with a task-conditioned gate on the final update.
one_sentence: Tabular foundation model pretrained on synthetic tasks with an in-context diversity prior and a looped ICL Transformer whose final pass is scaled by a task-statistics gate; more trained loops improve rank, extra test loops do not reliably.
key_contributions: Task-Conditioned Looped Transformer: shared ICL stack with scalar gate from support-set statistics
In-Context Diversity Prior for synthetic pretraining contexts
Loop depth ablations separating trained depth from inference depth

setup.model_sizes: twelve-block ICL Transformer, hidden width 512, looped L times; 2, 3, 4 loops tested
setup.train_tokens_or_data: synthetic tabular tasks; 25,000-step schedule on 64 AMD MI210 GPUs
setup.loops_test: matched to training; also 2 to 4 inference loops after two-loop training
setup.baselines: TabICLv1, TabICLv2, LimiX-2M, LimiX-16M and others
setup.benchmarks: six classification and five regression suites incl. TALENT, OpenML, PFN, TabArena

claims.claim: Adding diversity then the task-conditioned loop lowers average rank; the final comparison confounds loop and gate.
claims.regime: iso_data (same pretraining recipe); loop adds compute
claims.evidence_quote: According to the ablation studies, adding in-context diversity improves the rank from 2.40 to 2.17, and incorporating the task-conditioned loop further reduces it to 2.07.

claims.claim: More trained loops improve rank on some suites, with preferred depth varying by suite.
claims.evidence_quote: Increasing the matched depth from two to four loops improves the rank from 4.70 to 3.95 on TALENT and from 6.18 to 5.62 on OpenML, while PFN and TabArena favor three loops.

claims.claim: Running extra loops at test time on a two-loop-trained model does not reproduce the gain of training with more loops.
claims.evidence_quote: Additional inference-time repetition therefore does not reliably reproduce the benefit of training with greater loop depth.

claims.claim: Pretraining cost grows with loop depth.
claims.evidence_quote: Pretraining cost increases with loop depth: Taffy-4L requires 1.80× the backbone time per step

numbers.what: Average rank, extra inference loops: four loops vs two or three after two-loop training (428 shared entries)
numbers.quote: two and three loops both obtain aggregate ranks that round to 4.00, whereas four loops worsen the rank to 4.23.

numbers.what: Time per step of Taffy-4L relative to single-pass backbone
numbers.quote: Taffy-4L requires 1.80× the backbone time per step

limitations: Paper states the final ablation step evaluates loop and gate jointly; loop count is fixed, so the gate changes the update, not the number of steps.
builds_on: Yang et al. 2024 looped transformers in-context
survey_notes: Sec. 12 (tabular; survey currently cites LoopICL 2609.36108 only). Agrees with the survey line that tabular ICL suits looping, but adds that test-time loops beyond the trained count give mixed gains (rank 4.00 at 2 or 3, 4.23 at 4), unlike LoopICL which 'works at about twice its mean training loop count'. Cited sentence in Sec. 3 (not Sec. 12) 'Looped computation with task-conditioned gating' is the design motif.

title: GitSwarm: Decentralized Compounding Inference
relevance_reason: Multi-agent inference system; a Huginn architecture search is only one of its testbeds.
one_sentence: Asynchronous multi-agent Git-based system for accumulating inference-time work; one of three architecture-research tasks tunes the weight-tied Huginn model.
survey_notes: Out. Only relevant fact: agents improved a 308M Huginn variant by changing the recurrent input adapter (reported loss 3.187 vs 3.265 reference); not a looped-model contribution.

title: LoopMoEVR: Loop-Based Degradation-Aware Mixture-of-Experts for Unified UHD Video Restoration
relevance_reason: Shared spatio-temporal processing layers iterated K times (3 to 5, input-conditioned) on video features with MoE modulation.
one_sentence: Loop-based mixture-of-experts for unified UHD video restoration (0.884M parameters) with degradation-conditioned loop embeddings and an input-conditioned depth predictor; shared iterations match unshared at 71.6% fewer parameters.
key_contributions: Degradation-conditioned low-rank loop embeddings and IterAda3DN modulation with cross-iteration momentum
Depth predictor choosing 3 to 5 iterations
Highest mean PSNR on UHV-4K-AIO at 0.884M parameters

setup.loops_train: four iterations (restoration network), then depth predictor trained with network frozen
setup.baselines: MoCRA and other unified restoration models; LoopMoE-style video baseline
setup.benchmarks: UHV-4K-AIO dehazing, deraining, denoising, low-light; PSNR/SSIM/LPIPS/tLPIPS

claims.claim: At matched width and four iterations, sharing parameters across iterations costs only 0.08 dB PSNR and cuts parameters by 71.6%.
claims.evidence_quote: sharing reduces the parameter count from 3.116M to 0.884M, a reduction of 71.6%, with a PSNR difference of only 0.08 dB and a lower tLPIPS.

claims.claim: Input-conditioned depth saves inference time at similar quality and beats random depth allocation.
claims.evidence_quote: Dynamic depth saves 8.9% inference time over fixed four-step inference at similar quality and gains 0.51 dB PSNR over distribution-matched random allocation (Table 2(b))

claims.claim: Highest mean PSNR against a prior unified model with roughly four times the parameters (different training pipelines).
claims.evidence_quote: Table 1 shows that LoopMoEVR attains the highest mean PSNR with 0.884M parameters, exceeding MoCRA by 0.64 dB with roughly one-quarter as many parameters.

numbers.what: PSNR gain over LoopMoE-style video baseline
numbers.quote: The full model exceeds the LoopMoE-style video baseline (Chen et al., 2026) by 1.20 dB PSNR (Table 2(a)).

survey_notes: Sec. 12 (vision). Weight-sharing check at four iterations is iso-effective-depth and shows near-lossless tying (0.08 dB), consistent with the survey's 'tying versus untying' pattern in non-language domains. Caution: the abstract says looped paradigms are 'exemplified by GPT-6 and looped Transformers', an unsupported statement; do not cite it.

title: Loopy: Low-Bit Quantization Framework for Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: Systems work: post-training quantization of the shared recurrent core of looped LMs at the target recurrent depth.
one_sentence: Depth-aware PTQ for looped LMs: choose shared scaling and rotation candidates by final loss at the deployment depth with progressive full-depth evaluation; beats adapted SpinQuant and LoopQ on Ouro under W4A4.
key_contributions: Finding that best quantization configuration changes with recurrent depth
Target-depth objective solved by progressive calibration-window allocation using forward passes only
Evaluation on Ouro, Huginn and Recurrent-Llama under W4A8 and W4A4

setup.baselines: recurrent adaptations of AWQ, SmoothQuant, QuaRot, SpinQuant, FlatQuant; LoopQ (published results)
setup.benchmarks: WikiText-2 and LAMBADA perplexity; HellaSwag, WinoGrande, LAMBADA, ARC-Challenge, MMLU

claims.claim: The ranking of quantization configurations changes with recurrent depth, so calibration should target the deployment depth.
claims.evidence_quote: We find that quantization configuration candidate rankings can change with recurrent depth, motivating configuration selection at the target deployment depth.

claims.claim: Calibrating at the deployment depth lowers deployment perplexity on all three tested configurations.
claims.evidence_quote: increasing calibration depth lowers deployment perplexity in all three configurations.

claims.claim: Loopy reaches faster decoding than the official SpinQuant implementation on Ouro-1.4B.
claims.evidence_quote: online Loopy achieves about 41 and 41 decoding tokens per second (tokens/s), respectively, compared with 35 and 35 tokens/s for the official SpinQuant implementation.

claims.claim: Stated limitation: Recurrent-Llama degrades more under W4A4 and Loopy is not best there.
claims.evidence_quote: Recurrent-Llama exhibits greater degradation under W4A4 than W4A8, compared SpinQuant under W4A4, which is one of our work’s limitation.

numbers.what: LAMBADA perplexity reduction vs SpinQuant, Ouro-1.4B W4A4
numbers.quote: On Ouro-1.4B under W4A4, Loopy reduces LAMBADA perplexity by 36.5% relative to SpinQuant.

numbers.what: Ouro-1.4B W4A8 deployment perplexity, calibration depth shallowest vs deployment depth
numbers.quote: from 8.1184 to 8.0367 on Ouro-2.6B, from 12.83 to 11.41 on Ouro-1.4B, and from 9.98 to 9.79 on Huginn.

limitations: Recurrent-Llama under W4A4 is weaker; only recurrent-core linears are transformed; evaluations use simulated and kernel-level timing on one GPU class.
survey_notes: Sec. 8 (Quantization and numerics). Supports the survey statement that calibration must see later iterations; adds that the best candidate depends on depth and that the full-depth objective can be searched with forward passes only. Does not test the settling-versus-accumulation debate. Note: the Ouro-1.4B calibration-depth perplexities are token-normalized 2048-window numbers, not the main-table numbers. LoopQ (Fang et al. 2026) is a candidate missing paper if absent from the corpus.

title: Hybrid Latent Attention for Looped Language Models
relevance_reason: Systems work: KV-cache compression across loops for Ouro looped models.
one_sentence: Adds a sliding window of exact KV plus a per-token latent read directly by each loop to frozen Ouro-1.4B and 2.6B, cutting cache 10.7x per token and raising decode throughput up to 7.4x at 16K while keeping over 97% of accuracy.
key_contributions: Hybrid Latent Attention: exact window of W=128 tokens plus latents read without rebuilding keys and values
Uptraining with frozen weights (1,200 steps) and two-pass fine-tuning
Measurement against single-loop sharing and LLA under vLLM

setup.train_tokens_or_data: uptraining on attention distillation; SFT on math traces for 400 steps
setup.baselines: full cache, single-loop sharing (training-free), LLA with distilled codec
setup.benchmarks: MATH500, MMLU-Pro, BBH, RULER 4K-16K, AIME 2024/2025 and HMMT after fine-tuning

claims.claim: Cache shrinks 10.7x per token, fits 4.0-8.8x more sequences, throughput rises 2.5x at 1K and up to 7.4x at 16K.
claims.evidence_quote: The cache shrinks by 10.7× per token, fitting 4.0–8.8× as many concurrent sequences per GPU, and decoding throughput improves by 2.5× at 1K-token contexts and by up to 7.4× at 16K.

claims.claim: With frozen weights HLA retains 97.5-99.6% of accuracy on MATH500, MMLU-Pro and BBH and 96.0% of RULER at 16K for Ouro-1.4B.
claims.evidence_quote: On MATH500, MMLU-Pro and BBH it loses 0.3 to 1.8 points and retains 97.5 to 99.6% of the original accuracy.

claims.claim: Training-free sharing of one loop's keys and values collapses on Ouro-1.4B while a latent written from all loops does not.
claims.evidence_quote: On Ouro-1.4B its MATH500 accuracy drops from 75.9 to 45.9, with 44% of its generations reaching the length limit against 12.5% for HLA, and its RULER accuracy is at most 19%.

claims.claim: After two-pass fine-tuning HLA is on par with the fine-tuned full-cache model on competition math, within noise.
claims.evidence_quote: HLA reaches 16.4% against 16.2% for the full cache on Ouro-1.4B, and 28.0% against 27.2% on Ouro-2.6B, so its average is above that of the fine-tuned original at both sizes.

claims.claim: Single-sequence decoding is slower at short context; gains come from larger batches.
claims.evidence_quote: HLA is thus 26% slower at 1K, equal at 4K and twice as fast at 16K, and Ouro-2.6B behaves alike.

numbers.what: Per-token KV cache, Ouro-1.4B full vs HLA
numbers.quote: HLA shrinks the cache by 10.7× per token, from 768 to 72 KiB on the smaller model.
On RULER the loss grows with the context length, from 0.8 points at 4K to 3.1 at 16K for Ouro-1.4B, where it retains 96.0%

numbers.what: Throughput gain factors at 16K, Ouro-1.4B and Ouro-2.6B
numbers.quote: Throughput rises less than capacity: by 2.5 times at 1K for both models, and by 4.4 and 7.4 times at 16K.

limitations: Frozen-weight gap grows with context; contexts beyond 16K untested; one model family with T=4 and two sizes; fine-tuning tested on math only and needs two forward passes; speeds up generation only, prompts use exact attention.
survey_notes: Sec. 8 (The KV cache; Sharing caches; Huginn versus Ouro). Confirms that untrained single-loop sharing fails on Ouro (MATH500 75.9 to 45.9 on 1.4B, but only 7.2 points lost on 2.6B), and adds a trained latent that works at 10.7x. Survey statement to refine: 'Smaller caches do not make decoding faster by themselves, and they help throughput only by allowing larger batches' is supported (26% slower at 1K single sequence).

title: Towards Looped Models Done Right, Part II: Rethinking at Fixed Points
relevance_reason: Huginn-style prelude/recurrent-core/coda looped LM trained from scratch at 100M to 1.6B with fixed-point-based shortcuts.
one_sentence: Argues that near-fixed-point recurrent states let looped LMs use truncated BPTT, terminal KV sharing, distilled prefill and rollout-state RL reuse, and improves the fixed points with a learned depth prior and orthogonal input injection (100M to 1.6B).
key_contributions: Fixed-point view yielding four cost shortcuts: truncated BPTT, terminal KV sharing, distilled prefill, rollout-state reuse in RL
Learned depth prior with entropy term that preserves KV sharing
Orthogonal input injection (OrthoInj) that removes the carryover component along the input

setup.model_sizes: Small, Medium, Large scales from 100M to 1.6B parameters; layout 1+2xR+1 blocks
setup.train_tokens_or_data: Table 1 gives token counts per scale
setup.loops_train: depth prior over recurrences (PLN-5 baseline, learned priors capped at 64)
setup.loops_test: R=5 by default; deeper R in Appendix C.5
setup.baselines: Untied 4 (same parameters and KV), Untied 12 (same logical depth, 3x parameters), Huginn prior, Parcae injection
setup.benchmarks: validation perplexity, GSM8K, DROP, MBPP+, MATH500

claims.claim: Terminal KV sharing is nearly free for Huginn but collapses Ouro at four loops; the split tracks convergence to fixed points.
claims.evidence_quote: it barely changes the zero-shot GSM8K accuracy of Huginn [2] but collapses that of Ouro [5] at four loops [9].

claims.claim: Fixed-depth training with full BPTT does not form fixed points; KV sharing then halves its GSM8K accuracy at 1.6B.
claims.evidence_quote: Fixed-depth training with full backpropagation through time does not; at 1.6B, sharing drops its GSM8K accuracy from 50.6 to 21.2.

claims.claim: Learned depth prior with 3x smaller KV cache matches the full-cache downstream average of fixed-depth training at 1.6B.
claims.evidence_quote: At 1.6B, the learned prior with a 3× smaller KV cache matches the downstream average of fixed-depth training with the full cache.

claims.claim: Learned-prior looped model far surpasses a four-block untied model at the same parameters and KV cache and approaches a twelve-block untied model with 3x fewer of both.
claims.evidence_quote: The learned prior far surpasses Untied 4 at the same parameter count and KV cache, and approaches Untied 12 with 3× fewer of both.

claims.claim: Reusing saved rollout states halves RL scoring and backward time with small loss in GSM8K pass@1.
claims.evidence_quote: Rollout-state reuse (Section 3.1) halves the scoring and backward time of each RL update relative to replaying the loops with full backpropagation through time, and stays within 1.6 points of that baseline’s GSM8K pass@1.

claims.claim: Full BPTT at fixed depth fails fixed-point tests; truncation alone shapes the fixed points.
claims.evidence_quote: R = 5, full BPTT fails both: extrapolating to R = 64 raises perplexity by over 25%, and terminal KV sharing raises it by 21%.

numbers.what: Distilled prefill speed and gap to teacher on 8K prompts
numbers.value: up to 1.79x faster, trails by 1.0-4.5 points
numbers.quote: is up to 1.79× faster on 8K prompts and trails the teacher’s downstream average by 1.0–4.5 points

numbers.what: Distilled prefill vs teacher stopped at two recurrences, latency and accuracy
numbers.quote: it is 1–4% faster than teacher prefill at R = 2 and 0.5–0.9 points higher on the downstream average.

limitations: Models up to 1.6B with one seed per configuration; larger scales and other configurations untested; real-world feasibility needs study.
builds_on: Towards Looped Models Done Right Part I (blog)
survey_notes: Sec. 6 (Gradients through depth; Injection), Sec. 8 (Sharing caches; Huginn versus Ouro), Sec. 10 (Limiting dynamics). Updates the survey: truncation is not only a cost saver but the thing that creates fixed points that make terminal KV sharing work. Explains the Huginn versus Ouro split by convergence.

title: SanSi: A Looped Typed Decision Model for System 1.5 Thinking
relevance_reason: Turns a pretrained looped LM (Ouro) into a decision model read after every loop, up to eight loops.
one_sentence: Fine-tunes Ouro with per-loop LoRA and readouts so every loop from one to eight outputs option probabilities; eight loops add 13.5 points over a one-loop run at 7.7x compute, and unseen-depth synthetic tasks still work.
key_contributions: Per-loop proper-scoring-rule training so one model serves every budget from 1 to 8 loops
Controlled comparison of looped vs non-looped models of the same shape, plus newer and larger single-pass references
Depth-controlled tasks and a loop-8 judge for RL

setup.model_sizes: Ouro-1.4B (SanSi) and Ouro-2.6B (SanSi-2.6B), backbone frozen, 61M trained parameters for SanSi
setup.train_tokens_or_data: typed decision data; 10,027 test decisions from 59 sources
setup.baselines: SmolLM2-1.7B non-looped, same recipe; Qwen3.5-2B and Qwen3.5-4B; Kev-4B; Ouro-1.4B one loop
setup.benchmarks: JevBench-style typed decisions, liar chains, object swaps, RL judge F1

claims.claim: At the same shape, data and recipe, looping adds 13.5 points; the backbone alone is not the cause.
claims.evidence_quote: On 10,027 test decisions from 59 sources, SanSi reaches 72.0% accuracy: 13.5 points above a non-looped model of the same shape trained with the same recipe

claims.claim: Ouro run and trained with a single loop equals the non-looped control, so the gain comes from loops.
claims.evidence_quote: The backbone is not the cause: Ouro-1.4B trained and run with a single loop reaches 58.6%, indistinguishable from SmolLM2

claims.claim: Per parameter the looped model beats a newer single-pass model; per unit of compute a larger one wins.
claims.regime: unmatched (newer Qwen3.5 references are not controlled comparisons)
claims.evidence_quote: Takeaway. Eight loops add 13.5 points at fixed shape, data and recipe, paid in computation, not parameters. Per parameter, the looped model beats even a newer single-pass model; per unit of computation, a larger one wins.

claims.claim: Depth beyond training on synthetic liar chains: loops solve depths 9 to 16 where the larger single-pass model is at chance, but running more than the trained loops lowers accuracy on the mixed suite.
claims.evidence_quote: on liar chains of 9 to 16 steps (training goes up to 8), SanSi is right on 72.6% of the items and Qwen3.5-4B on 50.0%, the chance level.

claims.claim: Running past the trained eight loops hurts accuracy.
claims.evidence_quote: Running past the trained loops hurts (Figure 8): SanSi falls from 72.0% at loop 8 to 70.1% at loop 16

claims.claim: Used as the judge for RL, the loop-8 reading lifts the generator more than loop-4 reading.
claims.evidence_quote: Rewards read at loop 8 raise F1 from 39.5 to 47.3 (+7.7 [6.1, 9.4]) and at loop 4 to 45.8

numbers.what: Compute cost of eight loops relative to one pass
numbers.quote: and it costs 7.7 times the computation of a single pass.

numbers.what: Gap to Qwen3.5-4B at loop 8 and GPU time ratio
numbers.quote: Qwen3.5-4B, with three times the parameters, stays ahead: by 1.8 points [1.2, 2.5] at loop 8, where SanSi uses 3.3× its GPU time
The backbone stays frozen: we train only LoRA adapters and a small readout for every loop, 61M parameters in total for SanSi.

limitations: Builds on one family of backbones pretrained to loop (Ouro-1.4B and 2.6B); the gain relies on that pretraining; unseen depths remain unsolved; more loops than trained do not help.
survey_notes: Sec. 11 (controlled comparisons) and Sec. 7 (test-time depth). Another iso-shape, iso-recipe point where looping beats the non-looped twin (+13.5) but at 7.7x compute (not iso-inference-FLOP). Consistent with the survey claim that no language-model benchmark gains from loops beyond training depth, and adds a synthetic depth-controlled exception on Ouro.

title: RF-Agent: Hierarchical Language-Agent Control for Instruction-Conditioned Active Spectrum Sensing
relevance_reason: Closed-loop RF sensing agent; no weight-tied depth iteration.
one_sentence: Closed-loop RF sensing agent; no weight-tied depth iteration.

title: LatentIndex: Cross-Layer Sharing with Layer-Specific Selection for Sparse Attention
relevance_reason: Shares a latent indexer cache across layers in DeepSeek sparse attention; no shared block applied repeatedly.
one_sentence: Shares a latent indexer cache across layers in DeepSeek sparse attention; no shared block applied repeatedly.
survey_notes: Out. Cross-layer sharing of an index cache, not parameter tying. Possible one-line mention next to KV-sharing work in Sec. 8 only if the survey wants non-looped cache-sharing contrast (inference): none of its evidence is on looped models.

title: ALoDLM: Adaptively Looped Diffusion Language Models
relevance_reason: Within each denoising step a shared recurrent core (middle 16 layers at 8B) is iterated up to K=4 times with token-wise halting.
one_sentence: Converts Qwen3 into a diffusion LM whose recurrent core refines unresolved tokens for up to four passes per denoising step with learned halting; the 8B model averages 80.3 over eleven benchmarks and beats the Qwen3 AR models it started from.
key_contributions: Token-adaptive looped architecture inside each denoising step
Latent-variable exit schedule trained with conditional NELBO and a single-trajectory gradient estimator
1.7B and 8B models trained by SFT on 5B tokens

setup.model_sizes: ALoDLM-1.7B and ALoDLM-8B converted from Qwen3-1.7B and Qwen3-8B
setup.loops_train: maximum recurrent depth K=4; core is all 28 layers at 1.7B and the middle 16 layers at 8B
setup.loops_test: mean 1.6 to 2.34 loops per token by exit threshold q
setup.baselines: Qwen3 AR models, WeDLM, SDAR, LLaDA, Dream and other DLMs
setup.benchmarks: eleven benchmarks: ARC, MMLU, MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Diamond, GSM8K, MATH-500, HumanEval, MBPP and EvalPlus variants

claims.claim: Averages of 65.5 and 80.3 over eleven benchmarks beat the Qwen3 AR models at both scales; the AR baselines did not receive the same SFT, so this is not iso-data.
claims.evidence_quote: Compared to the strong Qwen3 AR models, ALoDLM presents consistent improvements on both 1.7B (63.8 vs. 65.5) and 8B scales (78.5 vs. 80.3).

claims.claim: Raising the exit threshold increases loops per token and the average score, so recurrent depth is a test-time axis.
claims.evidence_quote: increasing the exit threshold q raises the average number of loops per token from 1.6 to 2.34 and the average score across eleven benchmarks from 77.9% to 79.1%

claims.claim: Recurring over the middle layers beats recurring over the last layers at equal core size.
claims.evidence_quote: Middle-layer recurrence outperforms last-layer recurrence later in training,

claims.claim: K=4 reaches the quality of K=8 later in training while K=2 plateaus lower.
claims.evidence_quote: With half the maximum recurrent depth, K = 4 achieves comparable performance to K = 8 later in training, motivating our choice of K = 4.

claims.claim: Halting is lowest on numerical tokens, learned without difficulty labels.
claims.evidence_quote: Numerical tokens have the lowest mean halt probability (0.369), approximately 11.5% below the cross-dataset reference mean (0.417), while word tokens have the highest (0.428).

numbers.what: Speed vs vLLM-served Qwen3-8B on GSM8K
numbers.value: about 2.7x at comparable or higher accuracy
numbers.quote: ALoDLM-8B delivers approximately 2.7× the speed of vLLM-served Qwen38B at comparable or higher accuracy

numbers.what: Throughput and accuracy as entropy threshold tau rises 0.1 to 0.6 at q=0.5, GSM8K
numbers.quote: increasing τ from 0.1 to 0.6 relaxes the commitment criterion and raises throughput from 278.7 to 508.3 tokens/s, while accuracy decreases from 93.8% to 92.3%.

limitations: No limitations section found in the text; comparison with AR baselines is not iso-data (SFT on 5B tokens versus official Qwen3).
builds_on: LoopMDM / Lee et al. 2026 looped DLMs
survey_notes: Sec. 13 (Diffusion language models) and Sec. 12 (masked diffusion). Counter-example to the survey sentence that DLMs 'loop over the output and not over the hidden state of a token': ALoDLM iterates a shared core on token latents inside each denoising step. Claims 'the largest looped DLM to date' at 8B (authors' wording). Retrofit from Qwen3 by SFT (Sec. 6, building from checkpoints).

title: AdaLoop: Adaptive-Depth Latent Reasoning for Audio Language Models
relevance_reason: A shared Recurrent Latent Block iterated K times (halting, Kmax 8) over audio features before the LLM.
one_sentence: Replaces the audio-to-LLM connector with a shared recurrent block and ACT-style halting conditioned on audio and question; adds under 3% parameters and raises average accuracy 2.9 to 3.8 points on three audio LMs.
key_contributions: Recurrent Latent Block with question-guided cross-attention and scale-aware self-attention
Adaptive halting with ponder cost, depth set per audio-question pair
Plugs into three different audio LMs without changing encoder or LLM

setup.model_sizes: added module under 3% of base parameters; backbones Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, Kimi-Audio-7B-Instruct, MiMo-Audio-7B-Instruct
setup.train_tokens_or_data: 50,000 question-answer pairs from EvoAudio families; 1,000 steps then 3,000 steps
setup.loops_test: learned halting; mean 3.9 to 4.2 iterations on Kimi and MiMo
setup.baselines: Base, SFT of connector only, Fixed-4 (same block, fixed depth four)

claims.claim: Accuracy gains of 2.9 to 3.8 points on every backbone.
claims.regime: iso_data (same training data as SFT baseline); not iso-param versus Base
claims.evidence_quote: AdaLoop raises the average accuracy by 2.9 to 3.8 points on every backbone, and the learned depth distributions confirm that the model allocates deeper reasoning to perception-heavy tasks.

claims.claim: Adaptive halting is worth more than the extra loop count alone: swapping it for fixed depth four is the largest ablation drop.
claims.evidence_quote: Replacing adaptive halting with a fixed depth of four iterations causes the largest single drop (−1.7 points), confirming that the depth adaptation is the most valuable ingredient.

claims.claim: Question-conditioned halting matters.
claims.evidence_quote: Removing the question from the halting input (4) costs 1.6 points

numbers.what: Mean iterations on Kimi-Audio and MiMo-Audio
numbers.quote: Kimi-Audio averages 4.2 iterations (its weaker perception needs more refinement) and MiMo-Audio averages 3.9

limitations: Authors state that the ceiling is on tasks where a single coarse pass already suffices.
survey_notes: Sec. 12 (Speech) and Sec. 5 (halting policy). The loop sits in the connector over audio-encoder features, not inside the LLM, so it adds depth to the audio branch only. The Fixed-4 control is iso-architecture, which isolates halting from looping; no non-looped parameter-matched control is reported (inference from the baseline list).

title: CALR: Continuous Anchored Latent Reasoning via Render-of-Thought Compression
relevance_reason: Sequence-axis continuous latent reasoning; no shared block iterated in depth.
one_sentence: Anchors continuous visual latent reasoning to answers and derivations with a parallel-to-autoregressive curriculum; reaches 63.8% against 37.8% for Render-of-Thought on GSM8K-Aug with Qwen3-VL-4B.
key_contributions: Diagnosis that continuous latents influence answers but collapse content while discrete latents are bypassed
Functional anchoring with latent-mediated answer supervision
Parallel-to-autoregressive curriculum

setup.model_sizes: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct main; also Qwen3-VL-2B and 8B, LLaVA-Mistral-7B
setup.benchmarks: five mathematical reasoning benchmarks incl. GSM8K-Aug

claims.claim: Large gain over a comparable continuous latent method under matched latent budget.
claims.evidence_quote: unified autoregressive CALR achieves 63.8% versus RoT’s 37.8% accuracy with 32 continuous latents each, a 26.0-point gain.

survey_notes: Sec. 13 (Sequence-axis latent reasoning), comparison only. Priority 3.

title: What Matters for Latent Reasoning with Flow Matching
relevance_reason: Latent reasoning with flow matching in a learned latent space; its related work places looped models as the 'vertical' family.
one_sentence: Recipe for flow-matching latent thoughts probed against five requirements (useful, diverse, explainable, refinable, efficient); reaches 97% of explicit CoT accuracy at a quarter of its latency on arithmetic benchmarks.
key_contributions: Five requirements for a latent thought with a probe for each
FLaRe training recipe
Latency test against explicit CoT and prior latent methods

setup.model_sizes: VAE from Llama-3.2-1B and 3B; flow model Llama-3.2-1B-Instruct

claims.claim: Flow-based latent reasoning reaches near-CoT accuracy at lower latency.
claims.evidence_quote: while reaching 97% of the accuracy of explicit CoT at a quarter of its latency.

claims.claim: Authors classify looped models as one family of latent reasoning that applies the same layers over a fixed number of slots.
claims.evidence_quote: keep the number of slots fixed and apply the same layers over them several times, so the reasoning becomes an iterative computation within the hidden states

survey_notes: Sec. 13 (Sequence-axis latent reasoning and diffusion-style latents), comparison only. Their taxonomy 'horizontal / vertical / parallel' is a useful cross-reference to the survey's three recurrence axes.

title: Enhancing Long-Video VLM Embeddings with Query-Aware Streaming Latent Reasoning
relevance_reason: Clip-by-clip recurrent memory tokens for video embeddings; no shared block iterated in depth.
one_sentence: Clip-by-clip recurrent memory tokens for video embeddings; no shared block iterated in depth.
survey_notes: Out: recurrence over clips (time), no depth-looped shared block.

title: Continuous Memory Machines
relevance_reason: Nonlinear RNN with internal ticks and a shared memory Transformer; recurrence over time and ticks, positioned as a memory RNN, not as a looped Transformer.
one_sentence: Extends the Continuous Thought Machine with matrix-valued short- and long-term memory updated by a shared Transformer at every internal step; improves maze action accuracy from 88.8% to 96.3% at a 10M budget.
key_contributions: Separate short- and long-term matrix memories with a shared memory Transformer
Beats memory-augmented baselines on algorithmic and in-context tasks
Preserves CTM interpretable attention on mazes

setup.model_sizes: 10M parameter budget for maze task; 500K budget for other ablations
setup.train_tokens_or_data: algorithmic, in-context learning, maze, ImageNet-100 tasks
setup.loops_train: 50 internal steps on mazes; 25 on images
setup.baselines: CTM, CMM-LSTM, Transformer, RMT, other memory networks

claims.claim: On 39x39 mazes the CMM beats the CTM at a 10M budget.
claims.evidence_quote: increasing action accuracy from 88.8% to 96.3% and full maze accuracy from 37.4% to 61.6%.

claims.claim: Maze solving iterates the model over internal steps on the same input.
claims.evidence_quote: The model processes the maze over 50 internal steps, producing a full route prediction at each iteration.

limitations: Nonlinear recurrence restricts training parallelism; extra hyperparameters; memory Transformer applied at every step.
survey_notes: Sec. 13 comparison (memory RNNs with internal ticks, CTM lineage); borderline with recursive reasoning in Sec. 11 because ticks reuse parameters on the same input. Kept adjacent because the paper frames itself as a memory RNN.
